\subsection{A separately versioned implementation supplement}

Protocol 2.0 evaluates 4 selected implementation defects under 6 fixed conditions, with 128 independent clean calibration cases and 64 disjoint evaluation cases each (768 calibration and 384 evaluation cases in total). The ridge penalty is 1 and the lag window is 6. The comparison specifications and calibration assumptions are defined above; target-specific translation, NumPy agreement, and calibrated loss are experiment-only comparators. These selected fixtures are not an independent historical bug corpus.

The complete table retains the blind spots and false alarms of every comparison. These results concern these specifications and selected implementations, rather than the sensitivity of arbitrary metamorphic tests. In Study 2, corrected means the clean implementation refitted; the paired comparison is clean-minus-faulty, with no separate repaired arm. Any output-contract violation terminates the study.

Across the fixed condition--fault pairs, the calibrated loss alarm changed from no alarm to alarm in 861 paired comparisons and from alarm to no alarm in 11. The same clean case appears once per fault in these descriptive paired counts; they are not independent replicates of a pooled statistical test.

The clean implementation reduced mean realized MSE in 22/24 condition--fault pairs; 18/24 paired 95\% t intervals were wholly below zero. The full paired loss differences, intervals, and numbers of individually improved cases are retained in \code{model-repair-losses.csv}. These exploratory intervals are not adjusted across comparisons. Restoring implementation agreement need not improve every noisy realized forecast.

For random walk with drift with stale state, clean-minus-faulty mean MSE was +0.5132 [+0.2122, +0.8141] (paired 95\% t interval); only 21/64 realized forecasts improved. Restoring the declared algorithm can therefore worsen forecast accuracy on a particular condition.

\subsection{Negative controls and multiple covariance checks}

A second supplement evaluates 64 independent suites, each containing four conditional-reference covariance checks with 64 predictive trajectories, 199 calibration ensembles, and nominal level 0.05. The fixed variants are exact-reference samples, partial dependence permutation (strength 0.5), and spread multiplied by 0.75. Raw and Holm decisions are reported for the declared four-check families. Shuffled factorized white noise remains a negative control.

For clean suites, any false alarm occurred in 14/64 raw suites versus 3/64 after Holm correction. For reduced-spread suites, detection of at least one altered condition fell from 63/64 to 30/64. The correction thus reduces family-wise false alarms at a substantial power cost in this setting.

Coordinate-wise sorted sample arrays were identical before and after every partial permutation. The largest absolute marginal CRPS change was $8.88\times10^{-16}$. Paired energy and variogram score differences are retained for every condition. Correction can reduce power; every miss is reported. The covariance null remains IID trajectory sampling from the specified exact conditional reference, not general multivariate calibration of an arbitrary fitted model.

\paragraph{Cost and reproducibility.}

The retained study design requires 8,448 sklearn fits, 384 independent NumPy solves, and 768 covariance checks containing 152,832 calibration ensembles. Raw case records, protocol and source fingerprints, paired examples, and CSV tables are saved under \code{experiments/results-v2/}; the original pilot artefacts remain separate.
